state.purpose: Choose the commercial packaging for customer-specific offline AI cost-quality replay so first cash is fast but the same workflow can become stable recurring revenue and a transferable company asset.

priorFindings: V2 offline replay audit had the fastest time-to-cash concern at .27 and strong value ceiling .35 but weak recurrence and asset accumulation.
V4 recurring benchmark had stronger recurrence and very strong asset accumulation but slower initial cash and higher ongoing compute.
world.productKernel: fixed customer corpus/schema → replay selected models/providers → customer-defined quality + actual provider cost → cost-quality frontier + failure cases + reproducible receipt
world.marketReality: Models, provider prices and workloads change repeatedly, creating a natural reason to rerun the same benchmark.

candidates.name: one-off-replay-audit
candidates.claim: Sell one fixed-fee offline replay audit. Customer supplies bounded historical corpus and quality criterion. Factory returns reproducible cost-quality frontier, failure cases and projected savings. No recurring contract is designed until the customer explicitly asks for another run.

candidates.name: audit-to-annual-refresh
candidates.claim: Sell the same fixed-fee first replay audit with no platform build. If accepted, convert the exact same input/output contract into a prepaid annual refresh plan containing up to four reruns, triggered quarterly or by material model/provider/price/workload changes. Unused refreshes expire. No continuous monitoring is required and standard runs are automated.

candidates.name: monthly-benchmark-subscription
candidates.claim: Sell the first audit and immediately convert to a monthly subscription that reruns a fixed benchmark corpus every month across selected models/providers, maintaining version history and cost-quality trends. Standard runs are automated.

candidates.name: prepaid-benchmark-credits
candidates.claim: Sell the first audit, then offer prepaid benchmark credits that can be consumed whenever a model/provider/price/workload change justifies a rerun. Same fixed schema and receipt. Customer prepays a bundle but there is no calendar subscription.

constraints: Same core input/output contract across all candidates.
No production routing or effect authority.
No full SaaS platform before repeated paid demand.
Provider/model replay costs must be bounded in the paid scope.
No semantic PASS/FAIL threshold in Jev.
